answer: The grading quorum of 5 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so an adversary cannot sit on the panel that judges it. The tundra assignment is published and ferrous records each panel. Shards are assigned from the garden graph, which means cluster membership directly reduces grading power. A farm of 1335 identities would post 3272 proofs and burn roughly 35 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
